claim: Colorectal cancer ranks as the 3rd most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide in 2020 with 1,880,725 new cases.
source: With 1,880,725 new cases and 915,880 deaths, colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks as the 3rd most commonly diagnosed and 2nd most lethal cancer worldwide in 2020 (Sung et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sung et al., 2021, which provides the statistical data.

claim: Colorectal cancer ranks as the 2nd most lethal cancer worldwide in 2020 with 915,880 deaths.
source: With 1,880,725 new cases and 915,880 deaths, colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks as the 3rd most commonly diagnosed and 2nd most lethal cancer worldwide in 2020 (Sung et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sung et al., 2021, which provides the mortality statistics.

claim: It takes more than 20 years for normal colorectal mucosa to develop into metastatic carcinoma.
source: It takes more than 20 years for normal colorectal mucosa to develop into metastatic carcinoma.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about CRC progression.

claim: The 5-year survival rate of T1a stage CRC patients has been improved to over 90%.
source: Noticeably, endoscopic treatments enable radical resection of T1a stage CRC without open surgery, and the 5-year survival rate of those patients has been improved to over 90% (Li et al., 2019; Cao et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Cao et al., 2018.

claim: About 40% of AA patients could progress to invasive CRC within 10 years.
source: About 40% of AA patients could progress to invasive CRC within 10 years, which provided a very wide window of opportunity for curative treatment (Brenner et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Brenner et al., 2007.

claim: FOBT exhibited a sensitivity of 20% (95% CI 6.8% to 40.7%) for detecting AA.
source: The performances of FOBT and FIT to detect AA are especially disappointing, which exhibited a sensitivity of 20% (95% CI 6.8% to 40.7%) and 32% (95% CI 14.9% to 53.5%), respectively (Graser et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Graser et al., 2009 with specific statistical data.

claim: FIT exhibited a sensitivity of 32% (95% CI 14.9% to 53.5%) for detecting AA.
source: The performances of FOBT and FIT to detect AA are especially disappointing, which exhibited a sensitivity of 20% (95% CI 6.8% to 40.7%) and 32% (95% CI 14.9% to 53.5%), respectively (Graser et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Graser et al., 2009 with specific statistical data.

claim: A total of 58,333 annotated RNAs were detected from plasma sEVs, including 2,694 miRNAs, 24,927 mRNAs, and 30,712 lncRNAs.
source: A total of 58,333 annotated genes, including 2694 miRNAs, 24,927 mRNAs, and 30,712 lncRNAs, were detected.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results from RNA sequencing data.

claim: 1,615 sEV-RNAs were found differentially expressed in plasma from T1a stage CRC compared to normal controls.
source: A total of 58,333 annotated RNAs were detected from plasma sEVs, among which 1,615 and 888 sEV-RNAs were found differentially expressed in plasma from T1a stage CRC and AA compared to normal controls (NC).
evidence: This is a direct report of differential expression analysis results.

claim: 888 sEV-RNAs were found differentially expressed in plasma from AA compared to normal controls.
source: A total of 58,333 annotated RNAs were detected from plasma sEVs, among which 1,615 and 888 sEV-RNAs were found differentially expressed in plasma from T1a stage CRC and AA compared to normal controls (NC).
evidence: This is a direct report of differential expression analysis results.

claim: sEV-RNAs were categorized into six modules by weighted gene coexpression network analysis.
source: Then we further categorized these sEV-RNAs into six modules by a weighted gene coexpression network analysis and constructed a 60-gene t-SNE model consisting of the top 10 RNAs of each module that could well distinguish T1a stage CRC/AA from NC samples.
evidence: This describes the WGCNA analysis performed on the data.

claim: A 60-gene t-SNE model consisting of the top 10 RNAs of each module could well distinguish T1a stage CRC/AA from NC samples.
source: Then we further categorized these sEV-RNAs into six modules by a weighted gene coexpression network analysis and constructed a 60-gene t-SNE model consisting of the top 10 RNAs of each module that could well distinguish T1a stage CRC/AA from NC samples.
evidence: This describes the performance of the t-SNE model based on the experimental data.

claim: The optimized classifier achieved 79.3% specificity and 99.0% sensitivity.
source: Finally, we adopted different algorithms to improve the performance of RT-qPCR-based models and successfully constructed an optimized classifier with 79.3% specificity and 99.0% sensitivity.
evidence: This reports the performance metrics of the final classifier based on validation data.

claim: The sEVs isolated from plasma exhibited cup-shaped, vesicle-like structures.
source: TEM imaging showed that the sEVs isolated from plasma exhibited cup-shaped, vesicle-like structures (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is based on TEM imaging data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: NTA analysis revealed a heterogeneous size distribution of sEVs ranging between 75nm to 200nm.
source: NTA analysis revealed a heterogeneous size distribution ranging between 75nm to 200nm (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on NTA analysis data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Western blot analysis exhibited an enrichment of sEVs markers (CD9, TSG101, and Alix) and an absence of Calnexin.
source: Western blot analysis exhibited an enrichment of sEVs markers (CD9, TSG101, and Alix) and an absence of Calnexin, a negative marker of sEVs, indicating that the isolated fractions consisted mostly of sEVs (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is based on Western blot data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: An EV-associated RNA concentration of 3.70±2.39 ng per mL plasma was reported.
source: The total RNA levels of the sEVs fractions were also assessed, and an EV-associated RNA concentration of 3.70±2.39 ng per mL plasma was reported.
evidence: This is a direct measurement of RNA concentration from the samples.

claim: The top 100 miRNAs, mRNAs, and lncRNAs could roughly distinguish T1a stage CRC patients from AA and NC participants by unsupervised hierarchical clustering.
source: The top 100 miRNAs, mRNAs, and lncRNAs could roughly distinguish T1a stage CRC patients from AA and NC participants by unsupervised hierarchical clustering, respectively (Figure 2e).
evidence: This describes the results of hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claim: There were 888 DEGs between AA and NC, and 519 (58%) of them overlapped with DEGs between T1a stage CRC and NC.
source: Noticeably, there were 888 DEGs between AA and NC, and 519 (58%) of them overlapped with DEGs between T1a stage CRC and NC, suggesting most sEV-RNAs in AA remained abnormally expressed while progressing to T1a stage CRC.
evidence: This is based on the Venn diagram analysis of DEGs.

claim: Most sEV-RNAs in AA remained abnormally expressed while progressing to T1a stage CRC.
source: Noticeably, there were 888 DEGs between AA and NC, and 519 (58%) of them overlapped with DEGs between T1a stage CRC and NC, suggesting most sEV-RNAs in AA remained abnormally expressed while progressing to T1a stage CRC.
evidence: This is an inference based on the overlap of DEGs between different comparisons.

claim: DEGs were enriched in Pathways in cancer, MAPK signaling, Focal Adhesion.
source: KEGG pathway analysis suggested that those DEGs were enriched in Pathways in cancer, MAPK signaling, Focal Adhesion, etc., indicating a close relationship with cancer progression (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is based on KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2h.

claim: sEV-RNA of CC and RC showed higher expression levels of RNA markers of inflammation-promoting cells, MHC class I, HLA, TIL, and Paneth cells.
source: Especially, sEV-RNA of CC and RC showed higher expression levels of RNA markers of inflammation-promoting cells, MHC class I, HLA, TIL, and Paneth cells (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is based on ssGSEA analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: RNA markers of DC cells, Mast cells, and Enterocyte cells were mostly enriched in sEV-RNAs of NC and AA compared to those of CC and RC.
source: Correspondingly, RNA markers of DC cells, Mast cells, and Enterocyte cells were mostly enriched in sEV-RNAs of NC and AA compared to those of CC and RC (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is based on ssGSEA analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The sEV-RNAs of CC, RC, and AA exhibited significantly higher Immune scores and significantly higher Estimate scores as compared to those of NC.
source: The sEV-RNAs of CC, RC, and AA exhibited significantly higher Immune scores and significantly higher Estimate scores as compared to those of NC, whereas the NC group possessed the highest Stromal score (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is based on microenvironmental score calculations shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The NC group possessed the highest Stromal score.
source: The sEV-RNAs of CC, RC, and AA exhibited significantly higher Immune scores and significantly higher Estimate scores as compared to those of NC, whereas the NC group possessed the highest Stromal score (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is based on microenvironmental score calculations shown in Figure 3e.

claim: There is a higher proportion of inflammatory cell-originated sEVs in the plasma of CC, RC, and AA patients as compared to NC participants.
source: Taking all together, cell-specific features of the sEV-RNA profile indicated that there is a higher proportion of inflammatory cell-originated sEVs in the plasma of CC, RC, and AA patients as compared to NC participants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell-specific feature analysis.

claim: Six coexpression modules were constructed based on the expression levels of 1525 DEGs in each sample by WGCNA.
source: Six coexpression modules were constructed based on the expression levels of 1525 DEGs in each sample by WGCNA (Figure 4a).
evidence: This describes the WGCNA analysis results shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Most miRNAs were categorized into the brown module.
source: Noticeably, most miRNAs were categorized into the brown module, suggesting that the abundances of those sEV-miRNAs could be affected by the same factors, which further enhanced the necessity of including mRNAs and lncRNAs as additional biomarkers to cover as many patients as possible.
evidence: This is based on the module composition analysis shown in Figure 4c and 4d.

claim: The red module was significantly associated with endoscopic classification.
source: The red module was significantly associated with endoscopic classification (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is based on module-trait correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The black module was significantly associated with the endoscopic classification and the LST morphology.
source: The black module was significantly associated with the endoscopic classification and the LST morphology, while the green module was significantly associated with the LST morphology and the multiple-sited features (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is based on module-trait correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The green module was significantly associated with the LST morphology and the multiple-sited features.
source: The black module was significantly associated with the endoscopic classification and the LST morphology, while the green module was significantly associated with the LST morphology and the multiple-sited features (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is based on module-trait correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Flat lesions (subtype II) cases exhibited overexpressed MT-ND2 (blue module) levels in plasma sEVs as compared to protruding lesions (subtype Is/Ip/Isp).
source: For example, flat lesions (subtype II) cases exhibited overexpressed MT-ND2 (blue module) levels in plasma sEVs as compared to protruding lesions (subtype Is/Ip/Isp) (Figure 6b, left panel), while LST tumors showed a relatively higher level of HIST2H2AA4 (green module) than non-LST tumors (Figure 6b, right panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR validation data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: LST tumors showed a relatively higher level of HIST2H2AA4 (green module) than non-LST tumors.
source: For example, flat lesions (subtype II) cases exhibited overexpressed MT-ND2 (blue module) levels in plasma sEVs as compared to protruding lesions (subtype Is/Ip/Isp) (Figure 6b, left panel), while LST tumors showed a relatively higher level of HIST2H2AA4 (green module) than non-LST tumors (Figure 6b, right panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR validation data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The 8-gene signature exhibited an AUC of 0.76 for CRC prediction using Lasso regression.
source: The model with 8 sEV-RNAs exhibited an AUC of 0.76 (Table 2: upper panel; Figure 7a–d).
evidence: This is based on the ROC analysis results shown in Table 2 and Figure 7d.

claim: The highest AUC of 0.80 was achieved in the SVM model for CRC prediction.
source: Three different algorithms (logistic regression, Lasso regression, and SVM) were compared to further boost the performance of the 8-gene signature, and the highest AUC of 0.80 was achieved in the SVM model (Figure 7a–d).
evidence: This is based on comparison of different algorithms shown in Figure 7d.

claim: The 9-gene signature exhibited an AUC of 0.88 for AA prediction using Lasso regression.
source: Similarly, a model with 9 sEV-RNAs exhibited an AUC of 0.88 to predict AA from NC (Table 2: lower panel; Figure 7e–h). The Lasso model showed the highest AUC of 0.88 among all three algorithms, signifying an excellent efficacy in AA detection among noncancerous individuals (Figure 7e–h).
evidence: This is based on the ROC analysis results shown in Table 2 and Figure 7h.

claim: An overall accuracy of 78% (ranging from 63% to 100%) was obtained for direct sample classification using QDA.
source: An overall accuracy of 78% (ranging from 63% to 100%) was obtained for direct sample classification (Figure 7ij).
evidence: This is based on QDA analysis results shown in Figure 7i and 7j.

claim: The QDA classifier provided a specificity of 79.25%, and a sensitivity of 99.0% (with only one CC sample missed) in identifying high-risk individuals.
source: Generally, the individuals classified into AA/CC/RC are considered as high-risk and should be advised to further endoscopic examination, and our QDA classifier provided a specificity of 79.25%, and a sensitivity of 99.0% (with only one CC sample missed) in identifying those high-risk individuals.
evidence: This is based on QDA classification performance metrics.

claim: 2,694 miRNAs were identified in human circulating sEVs, including 1,838 known and 856 novel miRNAs.
source: Here, we identified 2694 miRNAs (1838 known, 856 novel), 24,927 mRNAs (18,947 known, 5980 novel), and 30,712 lncRNAs (12,928 known, 17,784 novel) in human circulating sEVs.
evidence: This is a direct report of RNA identification results from sequencing data.

claim: 24,927 mRNAs were identified in human circulating sEVs, including 18,947 known and 5,980 novel mRNAs.
source: Here, we identified 2694 miRNAs (1838 known, 856 novel), 24,927 mRNAs (18,947 known, 5980 novel), and 30,712 lncRNAs (12,928 known, 17,784 novel) in human circulating sEVs.
evidence: This is a direct report of RNA identification results from sequencing data.

claim: 30,712 lncRNAs were identified in human circulating sEVs, including 12,928 known and 17,784 novel lncRNAs.
source: Here, we identified 2694 miRNAs (1838 known, 856 novel), 24,927 mRNAs (18,947 known, 5980 novel), and 30,712 lncRNAs (12,928 known, 17,784 novel) in human circulating sEVs.

claim: A total of 2,621 RNA species showed a primary potential in distinguishing colorectal tumors from others.
source: A total of 2621 RNA species showed a primary potential in distinguishing colorectal tumors from others, which was a great treasury of biomarker candidates in liquid biopsy.
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis results.

claim: This is the first published whole-transcriptomic profile (including miRNA, mRNA, and lncRNA) dataset from human plasma EVs.
source: The profiling of circulating sEV-RNAs for early detection of CRC and AA we provided here, which is, to our knowledge, not only the first published whole-transcriptomic profile (including miRNA, mRNA, and lncRNA) dataset from human plasma EVs, but also the first attempt to simultaneously diagnose early CRC and precancerous AA by a plasma sEV-RNA signature.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: This is the first attempt to simultaneously diagnose early CRC and precancerous AA by a plasma sEV-RNA signature.
source: The profiling of circulating sEV-RNAs for early detection of CRC and AA we provided here, which is, to our knowledge, not only the first published whole-transcriptomic profile (including miRNA, mRNA, and lncRNA) dataset from human plasma EVs, but also the first attempt to simultaneously diagnose early CRC and precancerous AA by a plasma sEV-RNA signature.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: miR-425-5p was reported in promoting CRC via BRAF/RAS/MAPK Pathways.
source: For example, miR-425–5 p was reported in promoting CRC via BRAF/RAS/MAPK Pathways (Angius et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Angius et al., 2019.

claim: Hypoxia-induced let-7f-5p regulated osteosarcoma cell proliferation and invasion by inhibiting the Wnt signaling.
source: Hypoxia-induced let-7f-5p regulated osteosarcoma cell proliferation and invasion by inhibiting the Wnt signaling (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2020.

claim: Patients with higher PPDPF expression exhibited worse prognosis than others.
source: Additionally, patients with higher PPDPF expression exhibited worse prognosis than others (Mao et al., 2019), while high HIST1H2BK levels predicted poor prognosis in glioma patients (Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mao et al., 2019.

claim: High HIST1H2BK levels predicted poor prognosis in glioma patients.
source: Additionally, patients with higher PPDPF expression exhibited worse prognosis than others (Mao et al., 2019), while high HIST1H2BK levels predicted poor prognosis in glioma patients (Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2020.

claim: 31 early (T1a stage) CRC patients were enrolled for biomarker discovery, including 22 colon cancer patients and 9 rectum cancer patients.
source: For biomarker discovery, 31 early (T1a stage) CRC patients, including 22 colon cancer (CC) patients and 9 rectum cancer (RC) patients who received endoscopic resection at Department of Gastroenterology, Beijing Friendship Hospital between January 2018 and December 2019 were enrolled along with 19 AA patients (characterized by high-grade dysplasia or adenomas ≥10 mm or ≥25% villous component) and 10 non-cancerous (NC) outpatients with other gastrointestinal symptoms.
evidence: This describes the study cohort for the discovery phase.

claim: 19 AA patients characterized by high-grade dysplasia or adenomas ≥10 mm or ≥25% villous component were enrolled for biomarker discovery.
source: For biomarker discovery, 31 early (T1a stage) CRC patients, including 22 colon cancer (CC) patients and 9 rectum cancer (RC) patients who received endoscopic resection at Department of Gastroenterology, Beijing Friendship Hospital between January 2018 and December 2019 were enrolled along with 19 AA patients (characterized by high-grade dysplasia or adenomas ≥10 mm or ≥25% villous component) and 10 non-cancerous (NC) outpatients with other gastrointestinal symptoms.
evidence: This describes the study cohort for the discovery phase.

claim: 10 non-cancerous outpatients with other gastrointestinal symptoms were enrolled for biomarker discovery.
source: For biomarker discovery, 31 early (T1a stage) CRC patients, including 22 colon cancer (CC) patients and 9 rectum cancer (RC) patients who received endoscopic resection at Department of Gastroenterology, Beijing Friendship Hospital between January 2018 and December 2019 were enrolled along with 19 AA patients (characterized by high-grade dysplasia or adenomas ≥10 mm or ≥25% villous component) and 10 non-cancerous (NC) outpatients with other gastrointestinal symptoms.
evidence: This describes the study cohort for the discovery phase.

claim: 124 participants (47 CRC, 24 AA, and 53 NC) were enrolled for validation.
source: Additional 124 participants (47 CRC, 24 AA, and 53 NC) were enrolled for validation.
evidence: This describes the study cohort for the validation phase.

claim: Small extracellular vesicles are various-sized membrane particles of 40–100 nm diameter isolated by 100 K ultracentrifugation.
source: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) of 40–100 nm diameter isolated by 100 K ultracentrifugation were mostly considered to be exosomes, which derived from endosomes and participated in cell-cell communication (An et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to An et al., 2015 and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: sEVs derived from endosomes and participated in cell-cell communication.
source: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) of 40–100 nm diameter isolated by 100 K ultracentrifugation were mostly considered to be exosomes, which derived from endosomes and participated in cell-cell communication (An et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to An et al., 2015 and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The phospholipid bilayer of sEVs could effectively protect enclosed RNA from the RNase in the environment.
source: Additionally, the phospholipid bilayer of sEVs could effectively protect enclosed RNA from the RNase in the environment (Théry, 2015; Vlaeminck-Guillem, 2018), thus making sEV-RNA a relatively stable detection target.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Théry, 2015 and Vlaeminck-Guillem, 2018.

claim: sEV-encapsulated miRNAs outperformed their free-floating counterparts in diagnostic liquid-biopsy.
source: Previously, with a modified differential centrifugation (DC) procedure (Wei et al., 2020), we isolated sEVs from plasma and characterized those sEVs according to the MISEV2018 guideline (Théry et al., 2018). Then we proved that sEVs encapsuled miRNAs outperformed their free-floating counterparts in diagnostic liquid-biopsy, which proposed a new promising biomarker category (Min et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Min et al., 2019b).

claim: lncARSR in sEVs promoted sunitinib resistance in renal cancer in a ceRNA-dependent manner.
source: For example, lncARSR in sEVs promoted sunitinib resistance in renal cancer in a ceRNA-dependent manner (Qu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Qu et al., 2016.

claim: sEV-delivered HChrR6 mRNA showed a therapeutic effect in the treatment of human HER2(+) breast cancer.
source: Similarly, sEV-delivered HChrR6 mRNA showed a therapeutic effect in the treatment of human HER2(+) breast cancer (Forterre et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Forterre et al., 2020.

claim: The incidence and mortality of CRC in developing countries are gradually increasing due to rapid social-economic improvement.
source: Both the incidence and mortality of CRC in developing countries are gradually increasing due to rapid social-economic improvement (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2016.

claim: The mortality of CRC has dramatically decreased over the past decade in developed areas owing to the continuous improvement of multidisciplinary treatment and the promotion of CRC screening programs.
source: Even though a remarkably high CRC incidence was observed in developed areas, such as Europe and North America, the mortality of CRC has dramatically decreased over the past decade owing to the continuous improvement of multidisciplinary treatment and the promotion of CRC screening programs (Siegel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Siegel et al., 2017.

claim: Advanced adenoma is the crucial precancerous lesion of CRC, which is also resectable under endoscopy.
source: Advanced adenoma (AA) is the crucial precancerous lesion of CRC, which is also resectable under endoscopy (Hsu et al., 2020; Good et al., 2015; Tehranian et al., 2020; Shaukat et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hsu et al., 2020; Good et al., 2015; Tehranian et al., 2020; Shaukat et al., 2019.

claim: Endoscopic treatments enable radical resection of T1a stage CRC without open surgery.
source: Noticeably, endoscopic treatments enable radical resection of T1a stage CRC without open surgery, and the 5-year survival rate of those patients has been improved to over 90% (Li et al., 2019; Cao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Cao et al., 2018.

claim: Most AA patients were asymptomatic, and hard to be identified by opportunistic screening.
source: Unfortunately, most AA patients were asymptomatic, and hard to be identified by opportunistic screening.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about AA patients.

claim: The invasiveness and complicated operation procedures of endoscopy largely restricted its application in asymptomatic populations.
source: Endoscopy is the main approach for the screening of CRC and AA, whereas the invasiveness and complicated operation procedures largely restricted its application in asymptomatic populations.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of endoscopy screening.

claim: For most endoscopy screening programs, participants are simply pre-selected by their age and other epidemiological factors, resulting in low compliance and unsatisfactory cost-effectiveness.
source: For most endoscopy screening programs, participants are simply pre-selected by their age and other epidemiological factors, resulting in low compliance and unsatisfactory cost-effectiveness (Force, 2016; Sung et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Force, 2016 and Sung et al., 2015.

claim: The sensitivities of FOBT and FIT are far from satisfactory.
source: Fecal occult blood test (FOBT) and fecal immunohistochemistry test (FIT) are also popular in identifying individuals of high CRC/AA risk, whereas their sensitivities are far from satisfactory (Haug et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Haug et al., 2011.

claim: Circulating sEVs of T1a stage CRC and AA patients have distinct RNA profiles.
source: In conclusion, circulating sEVs of T1a stage CRC and AA patients have distinct RNA profiles, which successfully enable the detection of both T1a stage CRC and AA via liquid biopsy.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Distinct RNA profiles of circulating sEVs successfully enable the detection of both T1a stage CRC and AA via liquid biopsy.
source: In conclusion, circulating sEVs of T1a stage CRC and AA patients have distinct RNA profiles, which successfully enable the detection of both T1a stage CRC and AA via liquid biopsy.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental validation results.

claim: T1a stage CRC and precancerous AA patients retained a specific plasma sEV-RNA profile.
source: We also suggested that T1a stage CRC and precancerous AA patients retained a specific plasma sEV-RNA profile, which would provide insight into an in-depth understanding of the mechanism of CRC carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comprehensive analysis of the data.

claim: The plasma sEV-RNA profile would provide insight into an in-depth understanding of the mechanism of CRC carcinogenesis.
source: We also suggested that T1a stage CRC and precancerous AA patients retained a specific plasma sEV-RNA profile, which would provide insight into an in-depth understanding of the mechanism of CRC carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential implications of the findings.

claim: A comprehensive biomarker panel consisting of both plasma sEV-RNAs and proteins could be very promising in identifying both early and advanced CRC patients in the future.
source: Thus, here we also suggested that a comprehensive biomarker panel consisting of both plasma sEV-RNAs and proteins could be very promising in identifying both early and advanced CRC patients in the future.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the current findings and literature.

claim: Higher HIST2H2AA4 mRNAs in tissues could reflect a higher proliferation rate.
source: Considering the higher HIST2H2AA4 mRNAs and MT-ND2 mRNAs in tissues could reflect a higher proliferation rate and higher energy metabolism (Liu et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2009), their elevated levels in sEVs could be a potential indicator of invasiveness.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2020 and Sun et al., 2009.

claim: Higher MT-ND2 mRNAs in tissues could reflect higher energy metabolism.
source: Considering the higher HIST2H2AA4 mRNAs and MT-ND2 mRNAs in tissues could reflect a higher proliferation rate and higher energy metabolism (Liu et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2009), their elevated levels in sEVs could be a potential indicator of invasiveness.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2020 and Sun et al., 2009.

claim: Elevated levels of HIST2H2AA4 and MT-ND2 in sEVs could be a potential indicator of invasiveness.
source: Considering the higher HIST2H2AA4 mRNAs and MT-ND2 mRNAs in tissues could reflect a higher proliferation rate and higher energy metabolism (Liu et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2009), their elevated levels in sEVs could be a potential indicator of invasiveness.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the correlation analysis and literature.

claim: In-depth data mining of sEV-RNAs acquired by liquid biopsy would be helpful in different scenarios of healthcare decision-making.
source: Hence we believed that in-depth data mining of sEV-RNAs acquired by liquid biopsy would be helpful in different scenarios of healthcare decision-making.
